Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise Day0 checklist and the items we need from your side to keep the kickoff scoped to 45–60 minutes. If anything requires legal/procurement, flag it and we can route appropriately.

Day0 activation checklist (what Redwood needs before we run the activation sprint):
- Network: customer egress IP ranges + CIDR blocks to allow (we prefer a named list, e.g., catalyst-egress-1).
- Firewall rules: any inbound ports we should open; otherwise we default to outbound-only and mutual TLS for API calls.
- Service accounts: IAM role name(s) for our service principal + desired expiration/rotation cadence.
- KMS: KMS provider (AWS KMS / GCP CMEK / customer HSM). If customer-managed, share key ARN and IAM binding doc.
- Certs: if you're providing certs, share the CN/SAN expectations and staging certs for validation.
- Telemetry: sample retention window (logs/traces) and any specific masking requirements.
- Expected traffic profile: 95th percentile qps and average token lengths.
- Acceptance tests: baseline smoke test endpoints and a small prompt set for quality checks.

Security/compliance evidence we commonly request (we'll bring this to the kickoff checklist):
- SOC 2 report (if available) or equivalent attestations.
- Network topology + proof-of-control for any on-prem connectivity.
- Data retention policy and deletion SLA.
- Access control list for Day0 engineers (bastion + jumpbox accounts).

Next steps: send the network diagram and preferred kickoff windows. We'll confirm Rohit (on infra) and Karthik will own the runtime/ops checklist on our side. Vanessa will coordinate procurement/contract handoff if a PO/DocuSign is required.

Jonas Weber
Director, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
